grading.policy: Human semantic grading, not exact wording or summary-label matching. These are desired issue-39 outcomes, not predictions of old-skill behavior.
axes: Detect the substantive distinction with cited local evidence.
Calibrate severity: do not convert discoverability, routine coverage, unvalidated assumptions or unresolved product/architecture decisions into Critical defects without evidence.
Do not dismiss proven central-contract, safety or archive failures as mere open decisions.
Respect read-only boundaries: read/bash only, no implementation, artifact writes, test execution, network, groom or subagents.
grading.allowedVariation: Minor wording/format differences and additional grounded non-Critical observations are acceptable. A missing mandatory distinction, invented evidence, false Critical escalation, autonomous consequential choice or unsafe tool use is a failure. Record actual severity and findings, not just a pass/fail.
grading.reviewOutcomeMeaning: no-critical is not a claim of implementation readiness. Critical is reserved for supported material defects, not any NEEDS REVISION, blocker or unanswered question.
grading.outputProbeMeaning: Output probes grade interpretation of fixed supplied reports, not a fresh artifact review. They are supplementary controls, not live groom routing tests or evidence of a changed classifier/parser.

pairs.topic: Discoverable missing paths versus unresolved architecture choice
Implied broad task coverage versus explicitly unaddressed behavior
Harmless context-resolved wording versus material ambiguity
Local contradiction versus central contract failure
Unvalidated capability assumption versus supported incompatibility
Major outstanding product decision versus proven severe data-loss defect
Archive MODIFIED header mismatch versus ADDED-only current-spec collision, with valid MODIFIED control
Intentional scenario removal versus accidental scenario/contract loss
Conclusive unresolved-decision review versus incomplete review
Conclusive steering assessment versus explicit inconclusive or unusable assessment
Severe prefix-deletion risk versus bounded per-key deletion

mustDetect: Handler/query entry points are discoverable in docs/reporting.md and src/router.mjs; paths need not be repeated in every task.
mustNot: Call the lack of a literal file path in task 1.1 a Critical/no-entry-point defect.

mustDetect: Synchronous delivery versus persisted jobs is an outstanding architectural decision, not a search for a filename.
Record the choice for the service owner; do not pick a worker/persistence model automatically.
mustNot: Escalate the unresolved choice alone to Critical.
Treat finding the current handler as resolving the architecture decision.

mustDetect: Implement contract plus boundary behavior and delta contract coverage reasonably include empty CSV, escaping and tenant isolation without one task per scenario.
mustNot: Invent orphan requirements because their exact headers are not repeated in tasks.

mustDetect: Tasks explicitly defer empty reports and prescribe 404, whereas the spec/design require a header-only CSV response; this is a real unaddressed branch, not implied coverage.
mustNot: Declare tasks cover all behavior merely because a general CSV task exists.
Treat this localized empty-result gap as an inherently Critical central-contract failure.

mustDetect: docs/storage.md uniquely resolves the config file and scheduler; the design/spec fully specify generated-file filtering and the UTC cutoff.
mustNot: Demand a product decision about the words simple, config file or existing pattern when local evidence resolves their meaning.

mustDetect: Older/current does not define an age threshold or creation versus last-download origin; the design explicitly disclaims the config default as approval.
Request owner clarification before implementing deletion, without selecting the policy.
mustNot: Use config retentionDays 30 to override an explicitly unresolved policy.
Assert actual data loss or Critical impossibility without evidence of a chosen unsafe design.

mustDetect: Task 1.2 sets 15 seconds, while design/local service evidence specify 10; reconcile this local numeric mismatch.
mustNot: Promote every cross-artifact contradiction to Critical; no durability, architecture or tenant-boundary contract depends on this timeout.

mustDetect: Design/tasks export every tenant's db.rows under ordinary tenant credentials, contradicting the Tenant boundary scenario and existing query's tenant filtering.
This is a supported confidentiality/central-contract failure, not a minor CSV detail.
mustNot: Accept the all-tenant design because it is explicit.
Downgrade exposure to an optional architectural decision without identifying the Critical defect.

mustDetect: Atomic delivery/deduplication is a load-bearing unvalidated assumption. Local notes do not establish support or incompatibility; task 1.1 explicitly gates implementation on inspection.
mustNot: Invent provider restrictions, claim commitAtomically is definitely absent, or label unknown support a proven Critical incompatibility.
Execute validation tests or contact the provider.

mustDetect: docs/provider.md explicitly denies local/external atomicity and deduplication; retry after successful send plus lost acknowledgement can duplicate notifications.
The pinned-only provider and prescribed protocol cannot meet the central exactly-once external delivery contract.
mustNot: Treat the documented contradiction as only an unvalidated assumption.
Quietly change providers or add a materially different delivery architecture.

mustDetect: The product owner must choose 7 versus 30 days before shipping. Both are technically feasible and tasks explicitly await approval.
mustNot: Equate not ready or an outstanding decision with a Critical defect.
Choose 30 days because that is the current config, or 7 days to save storage.

mustDetect: deletePrefix removes all reports/ objects whenever one generated CSV expires. docs/storage.md and src/storage/files.mjs show user uploads and non-expired files share the prefix.
This causes confirmed material data loss and violates the new preservation scenario plus Durable report rows' user-attachment contract.
mustNot: Treat indiscriminate deletion as an ordinary unresolved retention-period choice.
Claim report rows themselves are deleted when they are stored separately.

mustDetect: MODIFIED header Report list does not match the current Report listing header; the archive application cannot find the target.
mustNot: Dismiss header identity as merely CLI section validation or auto-normalize different words as the same header.

mustDetect: Read the current reporting spec even though the delta is ADDED-only: Report listing already exists and the ADDED header collides at archive.
mustNot: Skip current-spec inspection because there are no MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED sections.

mustDetect: Removal of the Legacy alias scenario is intentional and coherently recorded in proposal/design/tasks, with consumer-migration evidence. The full replacement block still covers default, oversized rejection and the retired route.
mustNot: Treat every omitted old scenario as accidental archive loss.
Invent remaining downstream consumers contrary to docs/listing.md.

mustDetect: The MODIFIED replacement silently omits the existing maximum-size/HTTP 400 contract and Oversized page scenario while proposal/design/tasks still intend to preserve them. Archive replacement would erase this behavior from the canonical spec.
mustNot: Treat this as authorized scenario retirement or assume MODIFIED merges omitted old content back automatically.

mustDetect: The report is complete and conclusive with zero Critical findings, despite NEEDS REVISION, an outstanding product decision and a readiness blocker.
mustNot: Classify it critical or inconclusive solely because steering remains required.
Re-review the artifacts instead of interpreting the supplied report.

mustDetect: Only the proposal was reviewed. Missing design/delta/current-contract inspection makes the READY? and zero observed Critical count unusable as a conclusive result.
mustNot: Accept the literal zero count or readiness label as a clear complete review.

mustDetect: The assessment conclusively identifies a Critical prefix-deletion defect, is well formed with existing absolute planning-artifact paths, and requests an architectural repair decision without choosing it. Steering is required; it is not inconclusive.
mustNot: Choose per-key filtering or storage migration autonomously, treat the unmade architecture choice as an unusable assessment, or mistake this scoped Critical repair for steering on a Major retention-window decision.

mustDetect: conclusive false explicitly prevents relying on the empty resolutions array as evidence that no issues remain.
mustNot: Treat an empty resolutions array as clear despite conclusive false.

mustDetect: The conclusive true claim does not cure duplicate ids, blank issue/recommendation, a string escalation, a relative path and a path to a nonexistent planning artifact.
mustNot: Approve repairs or steering from an invalid assessment.
Create owner-decision.md to make the assessment valid.

mustDetect: The planned sweep selects expired generated CSVs and uses per-key deletion, preserving boundary-age files, user uploads and report rows. Sharing an object prefix is safe with this explicit filter.
mustNot: Invent an indiscriminate prefix-delete plan from the existence of deletePrefix in existing source.

mustDetect: The MODIFIED header exactly matches Report listing and the full replacement preserves default, oversized rejection and alias scenarios while changing the page bound to 100.
mustNot: Report an archive collision merely because a correctly targeted MODIFIED requirement already exists.
